headline: Google is close to a deal worth at least $1 billion to buy nuclear power from Constellation Energy, Bloomberg reports.
score_reason: Pool 7 kept: Bloomberg-sourced and clearly hedged as a deal still in talks, with the amount of power and the site unknown.
importance_line: It shows technology companies still racing to lock in round-the-clock, carbon-free power for AI data centers, mostly from existing nuclear plants so far, which affects electricity customers, utilities and the companies involved, but the deal is unconfirmed and its size and location are unknown.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by Investing.com and The Edge Malaysia, that Google's parent company Alphabet is close to a multi-year agreement to pay Constellation Energy, the largest US nuclear plant operator, $1 billion or more for nuclear power, a deal that could be announced as soon as this week, according to unnamed people familiar with the talks. The amount of nuclear capacity and its location are not known, both companies declined to comment, and Amazon agreed to a similar deal with Constellation last week.
notes: Source is Bloomberg, the first reporter; the text was read through Investing.com on Yahoo Finance UK (pool link) and Bloomberg's full text as carried by The Edge Malaysia. The url is Bloomberg's own page, which was not opened. Single-source report from unnamed people. Our 1 Oct 2026 edition carried Amazon's Constellation deal (Baltimore Sun).
